construct: SPAST encodes spastin, an AAA-family ATPase with microtubule-severing activity. SPAST dysfunction disrupts microtubule dynamics in long corticospinal axons and is the most common cause of autosomal dominant uncomplicated hereditary spastic paraplegia.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Pure autosomal dominant lower-extremity spastic paraplegia with a SPAST variant is SPG4; spastin is an AAA ATPase whose direct normal function includes microtubule severing/remodeling.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: PMP22 is peripheral myelin; SNAREs mediate vesicle fusion; lysosomal lipid degradation is unrelated; kinesin transport can be secondarily affected by altered microtubules but is not spastin's direct enzymatic function.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The lead explicitly asks the mutated protein's normal role, so microtubule severing is more direct than downstream axonal-transport consequences.
